context.why:
This is the last story of the feature, and it is what makes an opinionated default acceptable rather than a ceiling. US-1 to US-4 built a Plans page that a project gets without asking and cannot currently change. This story proves a project can replace it — the component, or the whole page template — and documents how.

Two of your six tasks are tests and prose about behaviour that very likely ALREADY WORKS. Django's app-directories template loader resolves a template by INSTALLED_APPS order, so a project application listed ahead of this package simply wins. Nothing was built to make that happen and nothing should need to be. If T028 passes on first run, that is the design holding, and it is the honest result — SAY SO PLAINLY IN YOUR REPORT rather than reshaping it into a conventional red/green cycle. tests/settings_with_project_template_override.py already establishes exactly how an override is tested in this repo, and tests/project_app/ already supplies one override template for the subscription page. Follow both; add to them rather than inventing a second mechanism.

The constitution amendment (T032) is the one piece of this story with real weight. Two sentences currently say, flatly, that a publishable key is 'never read from Django settings by this package'. Applied literally, the page US-1 built cannot work — and that page is the point of the feature, because a project that has to pass attributes is a project building the page itself. The amendment NARROWS each sentence to the COMPONENT, which genuinely never reads settings, and names the page reading settings and passing them down as the permitted shape. That distinction is the whole design: the component stays a pure function of its attributes, and exactly one place — the page — is allowed to know about configuration.

Put NO reasoning in the constitution itself. It states rules. The justification belongs in decisions.md, and you should write that entry.

prior_decisions: The override mechanism is Django's own template resolution order and nothing else. Do NOT add a setting, a registry, a hook or a swappable-class mechanism to support overriding — a project application ahead of this one in INSTALLED_APPS is the entire feature, and adding machinery would be building what Django already does.
The component remains a pure function of its attributes. The amendment narrows the rule to the component; it does not loosen it. Nothing in this story may make a component read settings.

The page is the one place permitted to read the two settings and pass them down. That asymmetry is the design, and T032's wording should make it read as a deliberate boundary rather than an exemption.
No reasoning text in CONSTITUTION.md. It states rules; decisions.md carries the why. Write the decisions.md entry for the amendment.
WATCH — T028 may well pass on first run, because nothing had to be built for it. Report which it was, honestly. Do not weaken the test to force a red.

WATCH — scenario 2 requires that EVERY context name the shipped page would have used is available to a project's own page template, and that those names are documented. Assert the names, do not assume them.
WATCH — scenario 3: either override renders with no view of the project's own and no query. Use the zero-query assertion, the way US-3's T016 test does.
WATCH — assert against rendered output, never against the presence of a class name (constitution Article XVI).
D10 — the demo's base.html loads pricing_table.js outside the provider-library block, and a test in tests/test_demo.py holds it there. Do not move it back and do not touch that file.
context.conventions: AGENTS.md — Development workflow. CONSTITUTION.md Article I (test-first), VI (public API changes ship their docs in the same change), VIII (every user-facing string translatable — gettext_lazy in Python, {% translate %} in templates), X (test modules mirror the source tree; Test<Subject> classes; component tests go under the declared non-mirror path tests/test_components/), XII (an interface layer and nothing else), XIII (no backend import, no provider script emitted, no build step), XIV (nothing at import time reads settings or reverses a URL), XVI (assert against rendered output, never against the presence of a class name). Public markdown — README.md, CONSTITUTION.md, CHANGELOG.md and docs/ are read by people outside this project: write plainly, no internal shorthand, no status markers, no revision stamps or strikethrough. Edit a document to read as current state; git records what changed.
